name: Audio Spectral Analysis
description: Analyzes audio spectral characteristics to detect synthetic artifacts, anomalies, and characteristic signatures of generative AI models.
algorithm: Audio Spectral Analysis — Frequency Domain Analyzer
mechanism:
This method performs spectral analysis of audio signals for detecting AI-generated speech following Chen et al. (2020):

1. **Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT)**: The audio signal is windowed and transformed to produce a spectrogram. The time-frequency representation reveals the full spectral content of the speech signal, including harmonics, formants, and noise components.

2. **Spectral Envelope Analysis**: The spectral envelope (smoothed magnitude spectrum) is extracted per frame using cepstral methods. Natural speech exhibits specific spectral envelope shapes determined by vocal tract resonances. AI vocoders (WaveNet, HiFi-GAN) may produce spectral envelopes with subtle artifacts — missing spectral detail above certain frequencies or unnatural smoothness in spectral transitions.

3. **High-Frequency Content Assessment**: Frequencies above 8 kHz are particularly informative for deepfake detection. Natural speech contains aperiodic high-frequency energy from fricatives and aspiration noise with specific spectral characteristics. Many AI voice synthesis systems produce truncated or artificially shaped high-frequency content, revealing the synthesis methodology.

4. **Mel-Frequency Analysis**: The spectrum is analyzed on the mel scale to capture perceptually relevant features. Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) and their delta/delta-delta derivatives are computed. AI-generated speech often shows statistical anomalies in MFCC distributions — particularly in higher-order coefficients capturing spectral detail.

5. **Spectral Flux & Continuity**: Frame-to-frame spectral changes (spectral flux) are measured. Natural speech shows characteristic flux patterns during phoneme transitions. AI-generated speech may exhibit unnaturally smooth spectral evolution or micro-discontinuities between vocoder frames, serving as detection indicators.
parameters:
Analysis type: frequency
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through audio spectral analysis analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Chen, T. et al. (2020). Generalization of Audio Deepfake Detection. Odyssey.
Chugh, K. et al. (2020). Not Made for Each Other — Audio-Visual Dissonance-based Deepfake Detection. ACM MM.
